tools.name: specs
tools.description: Call this FIRST in every session, before writing any uCAD script, even if you have notes or a skill about uCAD from before: the language (a small Python: every function, its arguments and the objects it returns, with the rules), how this service works, the reference examples, what is new. tools.name: example
tools.description: The script of one of the reference examples listed by specs (by its id): a finished model built carefully in uCAD's language, to learn from before building something like it.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Run a whole uCAD script on a drawing in the user's account (a new drawing when `drawing` is left out) and keep the result there. Returns the report (every solid with its size and place, warnings, print() output, or the error with its line), the drawing's id and link, and pictures of it. Each run rep

tools.name: view
tools.description: Pictures of a drawing as it is now (with anything the user changed by hand), from the sides asked for.

tools.name: scene
tools.description: What is in a drawing now: its solids and objects with sizes and places, flat shapes drawn by hand, and its script with line numbers.

tools.name: share
tools.description: A link to a drawing that anyone can open, with no uCAD account: they see the drawing as it is now (and as it changes later) in uCAD, and can turn it around, measure it, cut sections, download it and edit a copy of their own; its script isn't in it. Use it when the user wants to show or send the mode

tools.name: drawings
tools.description: The drawings kept in the user's uCAD account, newest first: id, name, when changed, link (and the link anyone can open, for those shared).

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: share · Public sink: share · Destructive: run_script.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: share · Public sink: share · Destructive: run_script

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
